text: The cutover load runs as a release-pipeline command under the rwb_payment service identity, addressed by the cutover record and not by a path; its command, its rights beyond the Platform administration R row, its run record and its scheduling are not published and are held open.
why: The legacy story states 'No endpoint in this story' and TSD P8 appendix T-A publishes two operations, both provided, so no source names the invocation of the load; the metadata H, C and X rows are empty and Ready to start is Day 1, so the load must be startable without a build dependency.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 DP-15 and DP-19, R5.7; legacy RWB-DM-013 Endpoints and Permission checks; TSD P8 v2 Appendix T-A.1; P8 context pack service facts
confirm: P8 solution architect and the release-pipeline owner at the contract review of RWB-P8-E2008-CON
impact: The load's entry point and run record are design choices until published; the criteria, the test cases and the data model do not change when they are named.

text: The cutover handover is one file produced by RWB-P1-DM013-APP for the payment owner, read once per run, carrying a row count, a checksum and one resolution stamp per row; its format, its location, its transfer channel and its retention are the extract's to name and are held open here.
why: The legacy story says only that the cutover reads the legacy records and that the breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract, and no source of this run fixes a file format or a location for the handover.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-013 AC1, AC2 and Endpoints; Template and Rules v1 R7.3 fill order; Work Package B2-P8-007 story line
applied_in: section 3, section 4, section 5 X1 and X3, section 12.8, section 13
confirm: rwb-source-data owner and the data steward before the first cutover rehearsal
impact: The reader and the fixtures assume one file with a count and a checksum; a different handover shape changes the reader and no criterion.

text: The migration provenance and the migration date of a loaded receipt are held in the standard record columns of TSD P8 T3.0 — created_by as the service identity and created_at as the load time — together with the legacy source name recorded in the load report, until the proceeds schema carries a named provenance column.
why: The legacy guardrail requires that a migrated record keeps its source and its migration date, while TSD P8 T3.1 and T3.0 model no column for either; the guardrail is kept and the columns are named so that no new column is invented.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-013 guardrails; TSD P8 v2 T3.0 and T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17
confirm: Schema baseline owner of rwb-payment at the next version of the proceeds model
impact: A provenance column in a later version supersedes the reading with no change to a criterion; until then the provenance is readable from the standard columns and the load report.

text: The legacy payment_code is kept as the payment reference and the business key of a migrated receipt, and account_payment_id is written only where the handover gives the ACE payment identifier; no foreign key is created into ACE and a row without the identifier is still loaded.
why: The legacy Data row keys the receipt on payment_code and TSD P8 T3.1 carries account_payment_id with no payment_code column, while RWB-P8-E2008-CON fixes the business key only where the environment grants it; a receipt without its reference would lose the link the legacy aim holds.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-013 Data and AC1; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.3; RWB-P8-E2008-CON section 12.7; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05
confirm: Schema baseline owner of rwb-payment and the rwb-source-data owner
impact: Where the identifier is absent the reference alone links the row; a later resolution adds the identifier without a new row and without a criterion change.

text: A second run of the load for the same cutover business date is a no-op: the row is keyed on the handover id and its payment reference, and the duplicate is refused by that key rather than by a run marker.
why: The legacy story requires ten clean days and a deterministic cutover, and TSD P8 publishes no idempotency key for a migration command; the key of the row is the only identifier both sources carry.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-013 AC3; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 DF-FIN-001 and Appendix T-A.2 idempotency row; RWB-P8-E2008-CON section 12.7
confirm: Solution architect of rwb-payment and the QA lead
impact: The repeat test asserts the row count and the keys; a different idempotency mechanism changes the writer and no criterion.

text: The metadata rows are applied exactly as the plan gives them: Status Draft (realignment v1) with no approval, release 31 December 2026 (tentative), wave 4 by the W-MAP of EP08 while the Arch v5 service row of rwb-payment is wave 2, and an empty H row although DP-15 and DP-19 name H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the sequence and the route are used and not built here.
why: No human approval is available in this run; R5.6 rules only on a W-MAP wave that is earlier than the service wave, so the later wave is kept and no conflict row is raised; R5.4 makes a contract row a build-time fake and never a blocker, so the two named H rows are read as declarations this story consumes rather than builds.
read: Template and Rules v1 R1 U7 and U8, R5.4, R5.5 DP-15 and DP-19, R5.6, R5.7 and R8.1; Work Package B2-P8-007 story line; P8 context pack service wave
confirm: Programme delivery lead at the C1 gate and the split-plan owner at the next plan version
impact: A later approval changes the status row and the release note only; a later plan version that adds the two H rows changes the readiness label and no criterion.
